radiology_report:
Antoni van Leeuwenhoek
Department of Radiology
Date: 10 February 2025
Exam: mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 12.0 ng/mL, prior negative biopsy, elevated PSA density.
FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 38.29 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal hypo-intense lesion in the left peripheral zone, approximately 12 mm in maximal diameter. This lesion shows restricted diffusion on DWI (high signal on b=1400, low ADC) and early, intense enhancement on DCE. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone metastases.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone. PSA density 0.313 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.8336016.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 7.6 ng/mL in August 2024, following a significant rise from 3.2 ng/mL in February 2024. Given the persistent elevation and previous negative biopsy, a repeat multiparametric MRI was arranged to guide further evaluation. The patient expressed considerable anxiety regarding the potential need for another biopsy procedure, and extra time was allocated to discuss the options and address his concerns.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1: The systematic transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy specimens were reviewed. No prostatic adenocarcinoma was identified. The Gleason score is reported as 0+0, corresponding to ISUP grade group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. No perineural invasion is seen.

Summary trajectory: The histological findings have remained stable across the single documented biopsy timepoint, with no evidence of malignancy detected.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
